slides.texte_overlay:
things you should stop
apologising for

being in the room

stop saying sorry for sitting down, asking a question or simply being there. you belong in that room just as much as anyone else, no permission needed.

needing a break

stop apologising for needing rest, help or a little time alone. everyone has needs, and saying yours calmly is healthy and normal, never selfish or weak.

not knowing everything

i stopped apologising for gaps in what i knew and started filling them a little every day. curiosity feels so much better than constant nervous apologies.
slides.texte_sophia:
not knowing everything

i stopped apologising for what i didn't know. now i take one lesson a day in the Sophia app, history or science, and every day i know a little more than the day before.

slides.texte_overlay:
changing your opinion

stop saying sorry for changing your mind after learning something new. updating your views isn't weakness, it's proof that you're still learning and growing.

saying no

stop apologising for turning down things you don't want to do. a kind no protects your time, and the right people will always understand and respect it.
